- Exact-reference verification status: Citation needed; exact supporting

## Proposal Text

Shape-memory alloys undergo reversible phase transitions that allow large
recoverable strains after deformation. Prior studies have shown that transition
temperature, hysteresis width, and cycling fatigue depend on alloy composition,
grain size, and thermomechanical history. These properties determine whether a
candidate alloy can operate reliably in compact robotic devices.

Our proposal builds on this field knowledge to design a low-fatigue actuator
platform.
